# Editor guide

A tour of the interface, ported from the in editor guided tour. Every command lives in the menu bar, grouped by what it works on: **File, Edit, Brush, Mesh, Texture, Terrain, Gameplay, Tools, View, Godot** and **Help**.

- Maps are `.gtm` files. Save them inside your Godot project so the addon can build them.
- The **grid** number is the grid size in map units. By default 32 map units are one meter in Godot.
- **CSG:** *Subtract* carves, *Merge* joins, *Intersect* keeps only the overlap, *Hollow* turns brushes into walls.
- Hold the **right mouse button** in the 3D view to look around and fly with **WASD** (Q/E down/up, Shift faster).

## The tools

- **Select** — the default tool for drawing, selecting, moving and resizing brushes.
- **Clip** — cuts brushes along a plane, for slopes, ramps and angled walls.
- **Vertex** — moves single corners and edges for shapes a box cannot make. Brushes always stay convex.
- **Rotate** — rotates the selection around its center.
- **Scale** — stretches the selection by its bounding box.
- **Mesh** — turns brushes into polygon meshes you edit like in Blender, for organic or detailed shapes.
- **Texture** — Hammer style texturing right in the 3D view.
- **Paint** — paints vertex colors on faces, for dirt, tint or fake lighting.
- **Sculpt** — shapes terrains and displacements.
- **Blend** — mixes materials: terrain layers, displacement alpha and blend material faces.
- **Scatter** — paints trees, rocks and foliage onto the surfaces you choose.
- **Volume** — drags out trigger and gameplay volumes in one step.
- **Path** — lays down `path_corner` chains for trains and moving platforms.
- **Measure** — measures the distance between two points.

## The panels

- **Outliner** — every layer, group, brush, mesh and entity as a tree. Click to select, the eye hides, the lock locks. Clicking a layer makes it the current layer new objects go into.
- **Inspector** — edits whatever is selected: entity properties and outputs, face materials and UVs, scatter sets and terrains. With nothing selected it shows the map's own settings (worldspawn): sun, sky and fog.
- **Materials** — the textures and materials of the Godot project. Click to apply, drag onto a face, right click for favourites.
- **Entities** — entity classes from the game config as cards. Drag one into a view or double click to place it at the cursor.
- **History** — every edit in order. Click an older entry to undo back to it, a later one to redo.
- **Issues** — problems in the map: invalid brushes, missing materials, outputs pointing at nothing. Click one to select the object, most offer a fix.
- **UV Editor** — edits the UVs of selected mesh faces directly.
- **Reference** — how to use the selected entity from code: GDScript and C# snippets, the FGD resource, and buttons that create the script in your project.

## Shortcuts and tips

- Hover any toolbar button to see its shortcut and a short explanation.
- Shift+click selects a single face, Ctrl+Shift+click adds more faces.
- Hold **Ctrl** while dragging the selection to drag out a copy, **Alt** moves it vertically in the 3D view.
- With the texture tool, **Alt+click** picks up a face's material and alignment and right click applies it elsewhere.
- **Ctrl+Shift+1..9** stores a camera bookmark, **Ctrl+1..9** jumps back to it.
- **Ctrl+= / Ctrl+-** scale the whole interface, the size is remembered.
- Opening a map that lives inside a Godot project loads that project too.
- Shortcuts here are the TrenchBroom preset. *Help > Keyboard Shortcuts* shows and changes yours.

## Into Godot

- Build a map with a `FuncGodotMap` node and **Build Map**. With the Godot editor open, saving rebuilds every map (**Auto Rebuild On Save**).
- For a running game, add `res://addons/func_godot/src/godottrench/runtime/godottrench_hot_reload.gd` as an autoload.
- The `GodotTrenchDebugOverlay` node shows fired outputs and trigger volumes. **F3** toggles it.
- Big maps stream via `chunk_streaming` / `chunk_size` / `load_radius` on worldspawn.
